territorial_scope.description: Applies to public and private schools of the National Education System under the federal education authority, with implementation by state education authorities and the Ciudad de México.

evidence.quote: de los tipos básico, medio superior y superior

summary.short: SEP Acuerdo 09/09/26 sets rules for students' use of personal digital devices and learning technologies in public and private schools of the National Education System. It restricts device use during the school day in preschool, primary and secondary levels, with listed exceptions. Enters into force 3 November 2026.
summary.long: The Acuerdo 09/09/26 of the Secretaría de Educación Pública sets conditions and practices for the use of personal digital devices and learning technologies in public and private schools of the National Education System. For preschool, primary and secondary levels (Art. 2) it restricts use of mobile phones and smart devices throughout the school day, allowing use only for programmed educational purposes under teacher guidance and for personal emergencies, disability, accessibility, inclusion, health needs or extraordinary community needs. For upper-secondary schools (Art. 3) it encourages responsible use and limits non-pedagogical use during the school day, through a school assembly and four listed modalities: classroom storage, limited times and spaces, no use, and scheduled use. For higher education (Art. 4) it encourages responsible and safe use according to community agreements. State education authorities must adopt the necessary measures and may adjust them, and must review implementation every semester with the SEP (Arts. 2-4, 6). Within 180 natural days after entry into force, state authorities must issue or harmonize legal instruments (Transitorio Tercero). Annexes 1-3 contain decálogos described as guidance proposals (Art. 7). The text sets no penalties.

notes: Registry gives DOF publication 22-09-2026; the document itself states only the signature date (21 de septiembre de 2026) and entry into force 3 de noviembre de 2026 (Transitorio PRIMERO), with DOF publication referred to without a date. Scope is inconsistent across provisions: Art. 1 covers básico, medio superior and superior, but the restriction in Art. 2 covers only inicial, preescolar, primaria and secundaria; Art. 3 (media superior) and Art. 4 (superior) only foster and limit use. The Art. 4 phrase 'durante toda la jornada escolar' does not clearly state a direction. Anexos 1 to 3 are described as 'propuesta orientadora' and the text says the approach is 'no desde la sanción'; no sanction provisions were found. Considerando references to UNESCO documents, the Convención sobre los Derechos del Niño, Agenda 2030, LGE art. 85 and foreign laws are context only and are not coded as relations.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changing legal treatment appears in the operative articles (Arts. 1-7) or transitorios. Art. 2 and Art. 3 differentiate by education level (basic, upper secondary, higher), not by number. The transitorio TERCERO 180-day period is a procedural deadline (events), not a threshold. The age of 16 for social networks appears only in the recitals, as a specialist's recommendation, not as an operative rule. Survey percentages in the recitals are descriptive and not coded. Annex decálogos are non-binding guidance.
